title: Operating them as a managed service: what changes and what does not

videos.script: Everything in this course so far, you ran yourself. You started the containers. You formed the replica set. You killed nodes and repaired them. {{lab}} A managed service offers to do that half for you. The machines, the patches, the failover, the backups. It is a real offer, and for most teams it is a good one. {{line}} But draw the line carefully. Above it sits everything about your data. The model, the indexes, the shard key, the consistency you ask for, the eviction policy. The provider runs whatever you choose, including the wrong choice. {{above}} Then two things the price page leaves out. A service compatible with MongoDB or Cassandra may be a different engine underneath. And the licence decides who may sell the software at all. MongoDB and Redis both changed theirs. {{licences}} Last, the exit. What leaving would cost in transfer, in downtime, and in features you came to rely on. {{exit}} No cloud account was used for this lesson. Nothing here was run against a provider, and nothing is shown that was not.
